topic: The 5-minute daily habit your heart will thank you for

scenes.line: Your heart wants five minutes from you. Today.
scenes.visual: Dr. Ira faces camera, warm smile, holds up five fingers; small heart icon floats by her shoulder
scenes.animation: Hard cut in. Big '5:00' pops in at upper third on 'five', scale 0.6 to 1, back.out; heart icon gives one soft pulse on 'Today'

scenes.line: Here's the habit: a brisk five-minute walk, every day.
scenes.visual: Teal walking-figure icon on a curved cream path, small clock badge reading 5:00
scenes.animation: Path draws left to right as the figure walks; clock badge counts 5:00 to 4:57 then holds; 'every day' underline sweeps in on 'every'

scenes.line: After lunch, after a call, whenever you've been sitting too long.
scenes.visual: Three rounded cards: plate icon, phone icon, chair icon
scenes.animation: Cards slide up one per phrase ('lunch', 'call', 'sitting'), stagger synced to words, power2.out; chair card gets a small walking-figure badge

scenes.line: Brisk means you can still talk, but not sing.
scenes.visual: Dr. Ira, friendly nod, one hand gesturing; speech bubble with tick on her left, music note with cross on her right
scenes.animation: Speech bubble pops in on 'talk', music note pops in on 'sing', each scale 0 to 1, 0.25 s

scenes.line: Regular activity like this can lower your risk of heart disease and stroke.
scenes.visual: Simple heart and brain outline icons side by side with a downward 'risk' arrow under them
scenes.animation: Icons fade up; 'risk' arrow slides down on 'lower'; heart outline does a slow, calm pulse

scenes.line: The goal for adults is about 150 minutes a week,
scenes.visual: Ring chart, teal stroke on soft-teal track, number in the centre
scenes.animation: Ring fills clockwise while the centre number counts 0 to 150, landing on the word '150'

scenes.line: and you can break it into small chunks.
scenes.visual: The full ring splits into small rounded segments that line up as a row of blocks
scenes.animation: Ring breaks into segments on 'break', segments slide into a row, stagger 0.06 s

scenes.line: So start with five. When it feels easy, make it ten.
scenes.visual: Dr. Ira, encouraging smile, small step-up gesture with her hand
scenes.animation: Chip '5 min' appears on 'five', morphs to '10 min' on 'ten' with an apricot highlight

scenes.line: Save this, and take your five-minute walk today.
scenes.visual: Dr. Ira points up toward a save (bookmark) icon, then a friendly wave
scenes.animation: Bookmark icon bounces twice on 'Save'; gentle fade toward the end card

scenes.visual: Cream end card with Pulse Health wordmark
scenes.onScreenText: Not medical advice. Sources: CDC, NHS
